snippet.description:
Apollo में 15%, Tata Steel में 7% की मार... 📉

Mega Deal के बाद भी क्यों मचा हाहाकार...⁉️

क्या पहले ही बाजार ने लगा लिया था सौदे का अंदाज...⁉️ 🤔

या Deal की Structure में छिपा है कोई राज...⁉️🔍

​🚨 Why APL Apollo & Tata Steel Crashed Despite a Mega Deal! 📉📊

​Two heavyweights on the screen right now are seeing sharp selling pressure, with APL Apollo sliding around 15–16% and Tata Steel dropping roughly 6–7% even after announcing a massive deal. While global metal stocks are under pressure, the sharp drop in APL Apollo despite a blockbuster structure makes this a story every serious market watcher needs to dissect carefully.

​In this deal, Tata Steel is selling two assets to APL Apollo for roughly ₹28,000 crore, while also moving to buy around 26% stake from APL Apollo’s promoters for nearly ₹15,500 crore and triggering an open offer for another 26% around ₹2,301—right near its life high of about ₹2,312—whereas promoters are exiting at around ₹2,100. Yet with the stock trading near ₹1,775, many investors are wondering why a seemingly attractive setup triggered immediate selling instead of a rally.

​There are two clear reasons behind the short-term reaction: first, the market had already anticipated parts of this deal, so news-driven profit booking kicked in right away; second, while shareholders get an attractive open-offer price, the funding loop around the ₹28,000 crore asset transfer makes the deal structure look tricky to short-term traders. However, from a long-term lens, shareholders get a high-price open-offer exit option, a major promoter like Tata Steel stepping in, and strong raw-material-to-pipe integration benefits.
​Short-term sentiment may stay jittery after the initial sell-off, so don’t chase knee-jerk moves blindly—share your view on whether this deal is a short-term trap or a long-term win in the comments below! 👇📈

snippet.description:

A Russian Navy frigate reportedly collided with a Russian fuel tanker during a refueling operation off Britain’s eastern coast, while intercepted communications allegedly revealed a crew member threatening to execute a fellow sailor over delays to the operation.

According to The Telegraph on November 21, the Baltic Fleet frigate Neustrashimy struck the tanker Valentin Rykov during an attempted refueling in the North Sea between October 21 and 23, 2026. The incident occurred near the coast of Essex, where rough seas and poor weather complicated efforts to bring the two vessels alongside each other. The frigate reportedly had enough fuel remaining for approximately two days of sailing.

Intercepted crew communications cited by The Telegraph indicated growing tensions aboard the Russian vessels as the refueling operation stalled. One sailor allegedly suggested taking an engineer to the ship’s helicopter deck and shooting him in front of the crew.

The reported threat followed disagreements over paperwork that had delayed the transfer of fuel. There is no indication that the threat was carried out.

The attempted refueling involved a maneuver known as rafting, in which vessels are secured alongside one another to transfer supplies. Such operations require careful positioning, particularly in rough seas.

Following the collision, the crews abandoned the initial attempt and moved toward the eastern coast of Scotland, where more sheltered waters allowed them to complete the refueling operation.

Both vessels reportedly switched off their Automatic Identification System transponders during the movement, limiting their visibility on civilian maritime tracking platforms.

The British Royal Navy patrol vessel HMS Tyne monitored the Russian ships throughout the operation, according to The Telegraph.

The Neustrashimy, a Project 11540 frigate assigned to Russia’s Baltic Fleet, had reportedly spent several months operating near British waters, including escorting Russian commercial vessels traveling through the English Channel.

Earlier, British forces monitored the same Russian frigate, Neustrashimy, during its passage through the English Channel between October 1 and 14. The Royal Air Force deployed its MQ-9B Protector surveillance drone on its first operational mission in British airspace, tracking the warship and accompanying merchant vessels for more than 10 hours alongside Royal Navy ships HMS Dauntless and HMS Tyne.

snippet.description:
PUTINS KRIEG IM ALL: Geheimdienste warnen vor Russischer Atomwaffe! Ex-Astronaut sieht enorme Gefahr

Krieg im Weltraum? Westliche Geheimdienste warnen laut Recherchen von WDR, NDR und Süddeutscher Zeitung vor einem möglichen russischen Satelliten mit Atomsprengkopf. Die mutmaßliche Weltraumwaffe „Sputnik-S“ könnte noch 2026 starten. Eine Atomexplosion im erdnahen Orbit könnte Satelliten zerstören, Starlink beeinträchtigen und Kommunikationsnetze gefährden. Ex-Astronaut Ulrich Walter erklärt die Folgen von Gammastrahlung, elektromagnetischen Impulsen und künstlichen Strahlungsgürteln. Zugleich äußert er Zweifel an Russlands möglichem Vorgehen. Moskau weist die Vorwürfe zurück.

#russland #putin #ukrainekrieg #weltnachrichtensender 

- Plant Russland eine Atomwaffe im Weltraum? Westliche Geheimdienste gehen laut aktuellen Medienrecherchen davon aus, dass Russland einen nuklear bestückten Satelliten namens „Sputnik-S“ starten könnte. Eine tatsächliche Stationierung ist bislang nicht bestätigt. Russland bestreitet die Vorwürfe. 
- Was passiert bei einer Atomexplosion im All? Eine nukleare Detonation könnte Satelliten unmittelbar durch Strahlung beschädigen. Zusätzlich könnten künstliche Strahlungsgürtel entstehen, die weitere Satelliten über längere Zeit gefährden. Ein elektromagnetischer Impuls könnte auch technische Systeme auf der Erde beeinträchtigen. 
- Würde eine solche Waffe auch Russland treffen? Ja, grundsätzlich könnten auch russische Satelliten von den Folgen betroffen sein. Ulrich Walter verweist im Interview ausdrücklich auf dieses Risiko und bezweifelt deshalb, dass Moskau eine solche Waffe tatsächlich einsetzen würde.

snippet.title: BÍ MẬT KỸ THUẬT ĐẰNG SAU HẦM THỦ THIÊM
snippet.description:
Hầm Thủ Thiêm nằm dưới sông Sài Gòn, nhưng phần vượt sông không được đào bằng máy khoan hầm.

Bí mật nằm ở công nghệ hầm dìm.

Phần hầm dưới sông dài 370,8 mét được chia thành 4 đốt bê tông cốt thép dự ứng lực khổng lồ, mỗi đốt dài khoảng 93 mét.

Các đốt hầm được đúc tại Nhơn Trạch, Đồng Nai, sau đó bịt kín hai đầu để chúng có thể nổi trên mặt nước.

Từng đốt được tàu lai dắt khoảng 22 km theo đường sông tới vị trí Thủ Thiêm.

Trong khi đó, dưới đáy sông đã được nạo vét tạo thành một rãnh đặt hầm.

Đến thời điểm dòng chảy và thủy triều phù hợp, nước được đưa vào các két để tăng trọng lượng, khiến đốt hầm từ từ chìm xuống.

Hệ thống định vị và các thiết bị điều chỉnh giúp đưa khối bê tông rộng hơn 33 mét vào đúng vị trí rồi nối với đốt trước đó.

Sau khi cân chỉnh, cát được bơm xuống phía dưới làm nền đỡ, hai bên được chèn lấp và phía trên tiếp tục được bảo vệ bằng các lớp vật liệu.

Bốn đốt lần lượt được dìm từ tháng 3 đến tháng 6/2010, trước khi toàn bộ phần hầm được hợp long vào tháng 9/2010.

Không phải đào một đường hầm xuyên dưới sông – họ chế tạo từng đoạn hầm trên bờ, làm chúng nổi như những con tàu rồi đánh chìm chính xác xuống đáy sông.
